page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-16xCPU-96GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 shared vCPUs powered by AMD EPYC 7542 processors clocked at 2.0 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, providing 6.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, and it does not include any GPU accelerators. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is provided.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The shared CPU allocation results in poor single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the bottom 10% and bzip3 single-threaded decompression rated as weak. However, multi-core operations perform at an average level, as demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 12409.56 and a PassMark CPU score of 28288.66. Memory bandwidth is average, reaching 48.36 GB/sec for large block reads and 28.85 GB/sec for large block writes.

This instance is suitable for workloads that can leverage multi-threaded execution to overcome single-core limitations, such as static web serving, Redis caching, and database operations, which scored in the average tier. It is also capable of handling light LLM inference for small models, though text generation on medium models drops to poor performance. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the shared CPU model offers a high density of memory and 16 vCPUs at a lower price point, making it a viable option for non-production environments, staging, and memory-intensive applications that do not require sustained, dedicated single-core CPU performance.
